input: candidates is a list of n positive integers in [1, 9007199254740991], with 0 <= n <= 100; duplicates and arbitrary input order are accepted. target is an integer in [0, 9007199254740991]. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh outer list of fresh nondecreasing value sequences, one for each distinct combination summing to target. Each input position may be used at most once, so multiplicity cannot exceed the input multiplicity. Equal combinations appear once. Output follows depth-first increasing-sorted-index order, skipping equal choices at the same depth. target = 0 returns one fresh empty combination, even for empty input; no positive candidate can extend that solution.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. Sorting uses a fresh shallow copy. Each accepted path is copied into a distinct mutable result container; no result aliases another, the input, the sorted copy or the temporary path. Values are immutable integers.
numeric: All values and remaining targets are exact safe integers. Subtraction occurs only after value <= remaining, so remaining - value stays in [0, 9007199254740991]; no potentially unsafe running sum is formed. JavaScript sorting uses a relational comparator returning only -1, 0 or 1. The bounded n limits recursive helper depth to n + 1 <= 101, not an unbounded recursion claim.
complexity: Let V be the number of recursive calls and R the result count. V <= 2^n and R <= V; each call scans at most n candidates, and copied accepted paths contain at most n values. Backtracking takes O((n + 1)*V) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary path/stack space and O((n + 1)*R) retained output space. Python copied sorting costs O(n*log(n+1)) time and O(n+1) auxiliary space. Positive values permit pruning at the first value above remaining. Duplicate skipping removes equal siblings, not legitimate repeated values deeper in a path.

helpers.name: collect
helpers.contract: A per-call closure over ordered, combinations and path. On remaining zero, copy the path; otherwise skip duplicate siblings, stop above remaining, choose one index, recurse from the next index with reduced remaining, then undo.
helpers.cost: The full helper definition is 536 UTF-8 bytes including indentation and terminal newline, already included in source bytes. All recursion, scanning and path-copy work is charged; at most n + 1 live helper calls. No memoized or external implementation.
